events.title: Deepwater Horizon disaster
events.description: An offshore drilling explosion kills workers and leads to a major oil spill.

events.title: Japan is struck by an earthquake and tsunami
events.description: Coastal communities suffer devastating damage and begin a long recovery.

events.title: Curiosity reaches Mars
events.description: NASA lands a large rover to study the planet.

what_happened_next.text:
All seven choices rose over five years. Amazon led this trio with a gain of about 358%, followed by Moody’s at 275% and AIG at 203%. AIG’s chart also includes an extraordinary jump in August 2009 and sharp falls at other times. Starting after a collapse can produce striking gains, but recovery was not guaranteed.

The companies’ businesses changed in different ways. Amazon’s fourth-quarter sales rose 20% to $25.6 billion in 2013 as its online store and cloud services expanded. Moody’s 2012 revenue grew 20% to $2.73 billion, with both ratings and data services contributing. In December 2012, the U.S. Treasury sold its last AIG shares and reported a positive return on the public rescue commitment. That public sale marked a recovery milestone; it is not a direct explanation for every AIG share-price move.

The next years included the Deepwater Horizon disaster, Japan’s earthquake and tsunami, and the landing of Curiosity on Mars. A percentage gain needs a starting amount: a share can rise greatly from a low point and still leave earlier owners far below their purchase price. This game begins in March 2009, so it does not include those earlier losses. The starting date is part of the story.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Government rescues, AIG bonuses and debt ratings drew scrutiny. Charities struggled, while companies still launched new products.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The starting point mattered greatly. These results begin after earlier crisis losses; they do not undo what an investor who bought much earlier had lost.
reflection.what_faded_away: A rescue headline did not promise gains for existing shareholders. Nor did a critic’s view of an electronic reader settle its company’s future.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The timing and strength of recovery were unknown. Large gains on a finished chart can hide the fear and sharp swings along the way.

hot:2009-03:aig.text: In December 2012, the U.S. Treasury announced the sale of its last AIG shares. AIG had sold businesses and cut its size nearly in half as it worked to repay its rescue. Focusing again on insurance helped it emerge as a smaller company after the crisis.

hot:2009-03:moodys.text: Moody’s 2012 sales rose 20% to $2.73 billion. More borrowing by companies created work for its credit-rating business, and its financial data and software business grew too. Operating profit rose 21%, so its higher sales were also bringing in more money after running costs.

hot:2009-03:amazon.text: Amazon’s sales for the final three months of 2013 rose 20% to $25.6 billion. It was expanding its online store and cloud-computing services, spending money to serve more customers. Sales growth showed rising demand, while the cost of that expansion also affected its profits.
